author: Henry Ketcham
claims: The power confided to Abraham Lincoln was to be used to hold, occupy, and possess the property and places belonging to the Government, and to collect the duties and imposts.
Lincoln ordered General Scott to employ every means in his power to strengthen and hold the forts.
Major Anderson was beleaguered in Fort Sumter.
Lincoln concluded to send provisions to Fort Sumter.
On Friday, April 12th, 1861, at 3:30 P.M., General Beauregard gave notice to Major Anderson that he would open fire on Fort Sumter in one hour.
The morning after the evacuation of Fort Sumter, Lincoln issued his call for 75,000 volunteers to serve for three months.
The government had decreed that at twelve o'clock noon on a specific day, the stars and stripes should be raised above Fort Sumter.
